description: We're RootSeekers, CS students from Karachi passionate about cybersecurity and building practical web tools. We're building a space-education web app/game for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Skills we have: web development, coding and problem-solving. Looking for: UI/graphic designers, storytellers/writers, and video/presentation help. Beginners welcome, bring curiosity and we'll learn and ship together in 48 hours!
summary: Moon Base Cadets is a free browser game for kids aged 7 to 12. Players run a base on the Moon or Mars for 10 days and must survive real solar flares and storm clouds from NASA's space weather records. Each day they share 10 units of power between air and food, radiation shields, and science. A day report explains whether the choice was good and why. On Mars, storm news arrives one sol late, which shows how communication delay changes decisions. After the mission, a debrief shows what really happened each day, with links to NASA records and a real NASA space biology study. There is no sign-up and no personal data is collected. The goal is to help young learners feel the trade-offs of life support, radiation shielding and power.
details: What it does: players pick a Moon or Mars base and play 10 days. Each day they allocate power between Air & food, Shields and Science while real NASA solar events (flares and CMEs) hit the base. Moon is easier because storms are seen before planning. Mars is harder because storm news arrives one sol late. Impact: it teaches kids that astronauts make real trade-offs, and shows real NASA data in a friendly way. The debrief links each day to its NASA record and a NASA OSDR study. Tools: TypeScript, React 19, Vite, zod, plain CSS, Vitest and Playwright tests, GitHub Actions CI, Vercel hosting. The game engine is seeded, so runs are reproducible. Creativity: kid-friendly space weather, a Mars communication-delay rule, and a "what really happened" debrief. Factors: no accounts, cookies or analytics; NASA data stored as labelled archived snapshots; science facts have checked sources.
